notes: Active ownership is determined only by a successfully created exclusive-scope lock.
Claiming does not change task status.
Tasks were seeded from the Premium Indie Gap Analysis dated 4 October 2026 and current player-feedback defects.
Tasks are role-owned through primary_agent. Agents normally claim only tasks assigned to their own agent number unless Josh explicitly reassigns the work or the queue is updated.
Supporting agents may advise or review but must not independently implement the primary task without a separate non-overlapping queued scope.

tasks.title: Immediate action feedback and meaningful button responses
tasks.goal: Every player-facing action visibly confirms what happened; no button should appear inert when state changes.
acceptance_criteria: Scavenge rope and salvage gives immediate visible feedback and cannot silently repeat unintended rewards.
Rest at the inn gives immediate visible feedback describing time/resource/health effects.
Hear rumours gives immediate visible feedback even when no new rumour is available.
Audit all interactive buttons for a visible success, failure, blocked, or no-op explanation.
Relevant feedback remains readable on phone-sized screens.
tasks.notes: Highest-priority polish/bug task from observed play.

tasks.title: Coherent visual identity foundation
tasks.goal: Create a consistent lightweight art/presentation layer without turning the game into a 3D project.
acceptance_criteria: Define reusable visual slots for party/NPC portraits, settlement/site art, enemies and items.
Improve map iconography and state readability.
Add restrained movement/combat/hit/heal/status visual feedback.
Assets degrade gracefully when unavailable and remain performant on mobile.

tasks.title: Audio and atmosphere foundation
tasks.goal: Give the Grey March a recognisable audio identity with optional, lightweight browser audio.
acceptance_criteria: Add opt-in/controllable ambience support for weather and key locations.
Add restrained UI/combat feedback sounds.
Persist mute/volume preference.
Respect browser autoplay restrictions and reduced-distraction play.

tasks.title: Make the four heroes into persistent characters
tasks.goal: Turn Garrick, Mira, Oren and Brindle from stat packages into people the player can become attached to.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce persistent character memories/traits or relationship state.
Add camp conversations and reactions to major decisions.
Support friendship/rivalry/loyalty changes without breaking old saves.
Provide hooks for personal quests and character-specific consequences.
tasks.notes: The premium gap analysis identifies personality/emotional weight as the biggest missing ingredient.

tasks.title: Visible world and faction consequences
tasks.goal: Make choices visibly alter the Grey March instead of only changing hidden numbers.
acceptance_criteria: At least several existing decisions alter later dialogue, services, prices, routes, danger or settlement state.
Faction changes have visible player-facing explanations.
End-of-campaign state can remember named decisions, not only renown/reputation totals.

tasks.title: Meaningful progression and builds
tasks.goal: Add build choices with trade-offs rather than linear stat growth.
acceptance_criteria: Define a small equipment or upgrade model that creates real choices.
Support at least one mutually exclusive upgrade decision per hero or build path.
Allow persistent injuries/conditions or transformations to affect play.
Save/load remains compatible.

tasks.title: Conditional authored event expansion
tasks.goal: Build memorable conditional travel/camp events that react to the party and prior choices.
acceptance_criteria: Event conditions can react to party members, traits/injuries, weather, factions, items, earlier decisions, time and quest outcomes.
Add a first curated batch of memorable events using those conditions.
Avoid filler events whose only effect is a generic resource roll.
tasks.notes: Blocked until character, consequence and progression foundations exist.

tasks.title: Strengthen the 18-day campaign arc and endings
tasks.goal: Turn the existing 18-day renown frame into a clearer escalating dramatic arc with substantially different endings.
acceptance_criteria: Define early, mid and late campaign beats without removing sandbox freedom.
Add a mid-campaign revelation and escalating faction pressure.
Add a hard late-game decision.
Endings reference specific consequential choices.

tasks.title: Phone-native interaction and accessibility pass
tasks.goal: Make Lantern Road feel intentionally designed for a phone browser rather than merely responsive.
acceptance_criteria: Improve one-handed interaction flow and choice sizing.
Verify map panning/zooming/touch targeting.
Add autosave and a clear save-slot direction without data loss.
Provide adjustable text size and high-contrast/accessibility settings.
Consider optional haptic feedback where browser/device support allows it.

tasks.title: Architecture and integration audit
tasks.goal: Audit Lantern Road's current architecture for fragile coupling, duplicated state logic, unsafe extension points and integration risks before the next wave of systems lands.
acceptance_criteria: Document the main runtime/state/rendering boundaries and identify high-risk coupling.
Remove or contain obvious architectural hazards where a small safe refactor is justified.
Define integration contracts for content, save state, UI feedback and feature modules.
Create follow-up queue tasks for larger refactors rather than silently expanding scope.
Existing gameplay behaviour remains intact.
tasks.notes: Steward-owned foundation task. Prefer small risk-reducing changes over a rewrite.

tasks.title: Save format versioning and migration hardening
tasks.goal: Make save/load resilient as character, progression, consequence and mobile systems evolve.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce an explicit save schema/version identifier.
Add a migration path for older saves rather than assuming the latest state shape.
Validate malformed or partial saves and give the player a useful recovery message.
Preserve current campaign data where safely possible.
Document compatibility expectations for future feature agents.

tasks.title: Runtime stability and performance baseline
tasks.goal: Establish a performance and stability baseline so new premium-indie features do not gradually make the browser game unreliable.
acceptance_criteria: Identify obvious repeated rendering/event-listener/timer or state-update hazards.
Check startup, travel, map interaction, modal flow and combat for runtime errors.
Add lightweight development diagnostics where useful without affecting normal play.
Keep mobile-browser performance in mind and record any measurable hotspots.
Turn significant out-of-scope findings into separate queue tasks.

tasks.title: Automated gameplay regression harness
tasks.goal: Create repeatable automated checks for Lantern Road's critical game loops so concurrent agent work can be integrated with confidence.
acceptance_criteria: Add automated checks for new campaign creation, deterministic state inspection and representative travel/action flows.
Cover save/load round-trip behaviour.
Cover at least one combat flow and one quest/site interaction.
Tests fail clearly on uncaught runtime errors or broken critical interactions.
Document how every feature agent should run the regression checks before PR completion.
tasks.notes: Steward-owned production-discipline task. Use the lightest practical test tooling for a static browser game.

tasks.title: Premium feature integration and consistency pass
tasks.goal: Integrate and reconcile the first premium-indie feature wave after the specialist foundations are complete.
acceptance_criteria: Audit cross-feature conflicts in UI, state, save data, content and pacing.
Ensure specialist systems feel like one game rather than independent feature patches.
Resolve duplicated patterns and inconsistent terminology/feedback.
Run full regression and phone-oriented smoke checks.
Record remaining premium-gap work as a prioritised second-wave queue.
tasks.notes: Blocked until the first specialist foundation wave is complete.

agent_roster.name: The Steward
agent_roster.role: Lead, architecture, integration, production discipline, cross-system consistency, bug triage and code review.

agent_roster.name: The Storyteller
agent_roster.role: Narrative, characters, dialogue, quests, consequences, campaign structure and endings.

agent_roster.name: The Mechanist
agent_roster.role: Combat, equipment, abilities, injuries, builds, economy, balance and deeper gameplay systems.

agent_roster.name: The Lamplighter
agent_roster.role: Art direction, UI feedback, animation, map presentation, sound, ambience and overall feel.

agent_roster.name: The Wayfinder
agent_roster.role: Mobile UX, accessibility, save/autosave usability, touch/map behaviour, testing, edge cases and interaction audits.
